sections.html:
The place to begin is the Official Records search run by the Pinellas County clerk and comptroller at mypinellasclerk.gov. Land records, deeds, mortgages, liens, judgments and plats are grouped together there, apart from court case files.

The clerk's records liaison is at 315 Court Street, Room 400, Clearwater, FL 33756, phone (727) 464-3341. The Customer Information Center number on the fee schedule is (727) 464-7000. A document that is not free online can be requested through the copy request center, which sends a quote.

Ownership, parcel and value data come from the property appraiser at pcpao.gov, with quick, map and advanced search for real property and tangible personal property. Use both sites: the clerk shows what was recorded, and the appraiser shows how the parcel is valued and who is on the tax roll.

The county holds 24 municipalities, and the appraiser's roll counts 437,624 real property parcels, 408,947 of them residential. That mix includes 241,442 single family units, 103,445 condo units, 22,112 townhome or PUD units and 44,323 manufactured home units.

Deed and records work is the same whether the parcel sits in a city or in unincorporated land, since one clerk records for the whole county. If you own a condo or manufactured home unit, ask the clerk which recorded documents apply to it.

sections.h2: Fees when a Pinellas deed is recorded
sections.html:
Recording fees follow state law, and the deed itself may owe stamp tax. The clerk posts a PDF at mypinellasclerk.gov/Home/Fee-Schedule that describes its charges as coming from statute, county ordinance and administrative order.

Under section 28.24(13) of the Florida Statutes, page one of an instrument up to 14 by 8.5 inches is $5.00 and each later page is $4.00. Extras include $1.00 per name past four, a modernization trust fund charge of $1.00 plus $0.50 per added page, and a technology charge of $4 per page.

Deed stamps in Pinellas are seventy cents for each $100 of consideration, the statewide rate outside Miami-Dade. Everyone on the deed is liable for the tax no matter who agrees to pay. Ask your closing agent for the recording total in writing before closing day.

  • Warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds are on the Department of Revenue's taxable list.
  • A deed from a personal representative acting under a probated will is listed as not taxable.
  • Divorce deeds for the marital home are exempt.

Section 689.01 calls for a written deed signed with two witnesses watching, and audio-video witnessing is allowed. No seal is required.

Other charges can land on the same closing statement. The clerk's schedule under section 28.24 shows $60.00 to process a tax deed application and $30.00 plus $15.00 per added page for plats. Mortgages carry 35 cents per $100 of the amount secured.

Recording protects the buyer against a later purchaser. Have the title company send the deed to the clerk on closing day, and keep the stamped copy.

sections.h2: What to look for in the recorded chain
sections.html:
Pull the chain of title and look for anything recorded against the property that the buyer's lender and closing agent will find. Common surprises are a mortgage that was never released, a contractor's lien, or a judgment filed under an owner's name.

  • Search the owner's name and the legal description, not just the street address.
  • Look for recorded mortgages without a matching satisfaction.
  • Look for liens, judgments and code enforcement filings.
  • Confirm the deed in your name was recorded and lists every owner correctly.

A 2020 Department of Revenue advisement examined a lady bird deed in which the life tenants kept full powers, and found that no present beneficial interest passed and no stamp tax was due on those facts. That guidance covers one fact pattern, so a title attorney should review yours.

Most transfers of title count as a change of ownership under Save Our Homes, with exceptions such as moves between spouses. A quitclaim to a relative can therefore lift the assessment to full value the following January.

A recorded document has a few parts worth reading slowly. The top shows who recorded it and when. The body names the parties and describes the property. A mortgage names the lender and the amount secured, and a satisfaction should reference the same mortgage. When a release seems to be missing, call the lender's payoff or records department and ask them to record one, because the title agent will not close until the old loan is cleared.

Names matter as much as numbers. A spelling variation, a missing middle initial or a former married name can hide a judgment from a quick search, so try several versions of each owner's name before you decide the record is clean.

Title companies work from the same public records you can search, but they read them with a checklist. Expect questions about every name that has held title, any open mortgage, any lien and any pending lawsuit that touches the parcel. Answering those questions before the contract is signed keeps the closing date from slipping.

If the house passed to you through a family transfer or an estate, tell the agent early. Those chains of title often include a deed or court document that needs a closer look, and a title attorney can explain what has to be recorded before a buyer's lender will accept the file.

First, run the searches above and print the results. Second, deal with whatever turns up: ask the lender for a recorded satisfaction, or ask the lienholder for a written payoff. Third, give the title agent the deed, any release documents and your exemption paperwork together. Fourth, after closing, confirm the new deed appears in the Official Records and keep the recorded copy.

A cash sale does not shorten any of this work. It mainly removes the buyer's loan approval, so it can finish faster once the title is clear.

faqs.q: Who is the recorder for Pinellas County?
faqs.a: The clerk and comptroller's office. It keeps deeds, mortgages, liens, judgments and plats, and its records page links to the search.

faqs.q: Can I search Pinellas County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Official Records search that the clerk's View Records page links to. Items not free online can be requested through the clerk's copy request center, which gives a cost quote.

faqs.q: How much is the documentary stamp tax on a Pinellas County deed?
faqs.a: Seventy cents on every $100 of price. Every county except Miami-Dade uses that rate, and the clerk collects it at recording.

faqs.q: What is the statutory recording fee in Pinellas County?
faqs.a: Section 28.24(13) sets $5.00 on page one and $4.00 on later pages, before the trust fund and technology charges. Check the clerk's PDF fee schedule for the current total.

faqs.q: Where do I find parcel and value information for Pinellas County?
faqs.a: Use the property appraiser at pcpao.gov, which offers address, owner, parcel ID and map search. The office has four service locations and a main phone line of (727) 464-3207.
